sections.name: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR

items.label: Group 1
items.notes:
- L1: BIO E 120A
- L2: BIO E 120B

items.label: 1 Specialization Group
items.description: Two courses required: Either a group, or 1 course from L1 and 1 course from L2

items.label: Approved Engineering Electives
items.description: Prior approval of the student’s departmental electives must be obtained from the student’s faculty adviser. Note, the list of approved electives may change from year to year and that not all courses are offered each year.
items.notes:
- ME W167 online version of ME 167.
- Four units maximum from ME 197 and ME 199 combined.
- Max of 1 TMP course may be applied

sections.notes: To satisfy major requirements, courses taken inside or outside the Department of Mechanical Engineering, must be taken for a letter grade.

nodes.title: Molecular Bioengineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 1
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1B or 3B, Chemistry 2AL, Math 6B, and Physics 7B
nodes.description: Introduces students to molecular components of biology with application of engineering principles for analysis. Topics include: molecular components of cells, DNA/RNA structure and function, protein structure/function/folding, gene and protein regulation, DNA replication, and experimental and computational research methods.

nodes.title: Cellular Bioengineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 1
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: BIOE 120A, or ENGR 120A, or consent of Instructor
nodes.description: Introduces students to structural components of cells with application of engineering principles for analysis. Topics include: biomembrane structure and function, membrane proteins, membrane transport, intracellular compartments, intracellular trafficking, chemotaxis, cell cycle, apoptosis, and stem cells.

nodes.title: Analytical Methods in Chemical Engineering
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI; Mathematics 6A or 6AI. Space may be limited, and registration priority will be given to Chemical Engineering majors.
nodes.description: Develop analytical tools to solve elementary partial differential equations and boundary value problems. Separation of variables, Laplace transforms, Sturm-Liouville theory, generalized Fourier analysis, and computer math tools.

nodes.title: General Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory).

nodes.title: General Chemistry
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: equilibrium; acids, bases, and buffers; thermochemistry (energy, enthalpy, entropy, and free energy); electrochemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: kinetics; intermolecular forces, liquids and solids; properties of solutions; transition metals and coordination complexes; organic chemistry and polymers; nuclear chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
nodes.description: The sequence of topics will be similar to that in Chemistry 1A. Calculus will be used as needed, at the level of the concurrent Mathematics 3A course.

nodes.title: General Chemistry Lab (Part A)
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A, or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-. Concurrent enrollment, or a grade of C- or higher in CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B, or CHEM 3B.
nodes.description: Qualitative and quantitative measurements to develop laboratory techniques and demonstrate the basic concepts of stoichiometry, gas laws, atomic spectroscopy, chemical equilibrium, and acid-base chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 2A or CHEM 1A or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of B.
nodes.description: Thermodynamics (first and second law), electrochemistry, chemical kinetics, atomic and molecular structure, and chemical bonding.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Honors)
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 2B or CHEM 1B or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of B.
nodes.description: Structure and dynamics of the elements and their compounds. Aspects of technology and environmental problems.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
nodes.prereq_text: None
nodes.description: Topics covered: atomic structure of matter; reaction stoichiometry; solution stoichiometry; gasses; quantum chemistry and the electronic structure of atoms; chemical bonding (molecular shapes, hybridization, and molecular orbital theory). First quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1A, CHEM 2A, or CHEM 3A with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: equilibrium; acids, bases, and buffers; thermochemistry (energy, enthalpy, entropy, and free energy); electrochemistry. Second quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

nodes.title: General Chemistry (Majors)
nodes.prereq_text: CHEM 1B, CHEM 2B, or CHEM 3B with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Topics covered: kinetics; intermolecular forces, liquids and solids; properties of solutions; transition metals and coordination complexes; organic chemistry and polymers; nuclear chemistry. Third quarter of general chemistry intended for Chemistry Pre-Majors and Chemical Engineering Majors and others requiring a strong basis in chemistry.

nodes.title: Organic Chemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1C or 2C or 3C with a minimum grade of C-; or Chemistry 1B or 2B or 3B with a minimum grade of B-.
nodes.description: Introduction to organic chemistry. Topics include acid/base chemistry, conformational analysis, stereoisomers, thermodynamics and kinetics, aromaticity and resonance, and multistep synthesis as well as the nomenclature, structure, reactivity, and mechanisms of alkenes, alkynes, and alkyl halides. Reaction mechanisms include electrophilic addition, substitution, and elimination reactions.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Environmental Chemistry
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B.
nodes.description: Study of Earth's biogeochemical cycles with respect to carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur. Introduction to the science of climate change, including effects of global warming on terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. Environmental impacts of fossil fuel and biofuel technologies. Chemistry of the atmosphere, hydrosphere, and lithosphere, with emphasis on ozone depletion, photochemical smog, acid rain, global ocean acidification, soil and groundwater contamination, and environmental costs of industrialized agriculture.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Vision
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.
nodes.description: Overview of computer vision problems and techniques for analyzing the content of images and video. Topics include image formation, edge detection, image segmentation, pattern recognition, texture analysis, optical flow, stereo vision, shape representation and recovery techniques, issues in object recognition, and case studies of practical vision systems.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits & Systems
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or Mathematics 3AH-BH, and Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 3C, all with a minimum grade of C; and, Math 4B or 4BI or 5A with a minimum grade of C (may be taken concurrently); Physics 3, 7B or 23 (may be taken concurrently); open only to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors.

items.text: open only to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors

nodes.description: The objective of the course is to establish the foundations of analog and digital circuits. The course will introduce the student to the power of abstraction, resistive networks, network analysis, nonlinear analysis and the digital abstraction.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems Lab
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10A (may be taken concurrently) with a C- or better grade.
nodes.description: The goal of 10AL is to provide the student with a hands-on application of the concepts discussed in ECE 10A. The lab will introduce the use of microcontrollers as a data acquisition system, network analysis, resistors, nonlinear analysis and digital abstraction.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10A with a C- or better grade.
nodes.description: The objective of the course is to introduce the MOSFET both as a simple digital switch and as controlled current source for analog design. The course will cover basic digital design, small-signal analysis, charge storage elements and operational amplifiers.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems Lab
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10B (may be taken concurrently) with a C- or better grade.
nodes.description: The goal of 10BL is to provide the student with a hands-on application of the concepts discussed in ECE 10B. The lab will utilize the microcontroller to introduce students to the understanding of datasheets for both digital and analog circuits, single-stage amplifier design and basic instrumentation.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10B with a C- or better grade.
nodes.description: The objective of the course is to introduce the student to the basics of transient analysis. The course will energy and power dissipation in digital circuits, first-order and second-order linear time invariant circuits, sinusoidal steady state, impedance representation, feedback and resonance.

nodes.title: Foundations of Analog and Digital Circuits and Systems Lab
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10C (may be taken concurrently) with a C- grade or better.
nodes.description: The goal of 10CL is to provide the student with a hands-on application of the concepts discussed in ECE 10C. The lab will utilize the microcontroller to introduce students to the understanding of propagation delay in digital circuits and the resulting power dissipation, first order linear networks, second order linear networks, sinusoidal steady-state, impedance analysis and op-amp circuits.

nodes.title: Signal Analysis and Processing
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B or 5A with a minimum of grade of C; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to EE and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Analysis of continuous time linear systems in the time and frequency domains. Superposition and convolution. Bilateral and unilateral Laplace transforms. Fourier series and Fourier transforms. Filtering, modulation, and feedback.

nodes.title: Signal Analysis and Processing
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 130A with a minimum grade of C- or better; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to EE and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Analysis of discrete time linear systems in the time and frequency domains. Z transforms, Discrete Fourier transforms. Sampling and aliasing.

nodes.title: Introduction to Solid-State Electronic Devices
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 4 or 24 or 7D with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4B, 4BI or 5A with a minimum grade of C; open to EE and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to EE and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Electrons and holes in semiconductors; doping (P and N); state occupation statistics, transport properties of electrons and holes; P-N junction diodes; I-V, C-V, and switching properties of P-N junctions; introduction of bipolar transitors, MOSFET's and JFET's.

nodes.title: Circuits and Electronics I
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 10A-B-C and 10AL-BL-CL or 2A-B-C, 130A and 132 all with a minimum grade of C-; open to EE majors only.
nodes.description: Analysis and design of single stage and multistage transistor circuits including biasing, gain, impedances and maximum signal levels.

nodes.title: Introduction to Nanoelectromechanical and Microelectromechanical systems (NEMS/MEMS)
nodes.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16 and 17; ME 152A and ME 151A (may be concurrent); or ECE 130A & 137A with a minimum grade of C- in both.
nodes.description: Introduction to nano- and microtechnology. Scaling laws and nanoscale physics are stressed. Individual subjects at the nanoscale including materials, mechanics, photonics, electronics, and fluidics will be described, with an emphasis on differences of behavior at the nanoscale and real-world examples.

nodes.title: Feedback Control Systems - Theory and Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 130A-B with a minimum grade of C- in each; open to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors only.

items.text: open to electrical engineering and computer engineering majors only

nodes.description: Feedback systems design, specifications in time and frequency domains. Analysis and synthesis of closed loope systems. Computer aided analysis anddesign.

nodes.title: Control System Design Project
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 147A or ME 155B or ME 173 with a minimum grade of C-.
nodes.description: Students are required to design, implement, and document a significant control systems project. The project is implemented in hardware or in high-fidelity numerical simulators. Lectures and laboratories cover special topics related to the practical implementation of control systems.

nodes.title: Introduction to Computer Vision
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.
nodes.description: Overview of computer vision problems and techniques for analyzing the content of images and video. Topics include image formation, edge detection, image segmentation, pattern recognition, texture analysis, optical flow, stereo vision, shape representation and recovery techniques, issues in object recognition, and case studies of practical vision systems.

nodes.title: Introduction to Programming
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.description: General philosophy of programming and problem-solving. Students will be introduced to the programming language MATLAB. Specific areas of study will include algorithms, basic decision structures, arrays, matrices, and graphing.

nodes.title: Ethics in Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Senior standing in engineering.
nodes.description: The nature of moral value, normative judgment and moral reasoning. Theories of moral value. The engineer's role in society. Ethics in professional practice. Safety, risk, responsibility. Morality and career choice. Code of ethics. Case studies facilitate the comprehension of the concepts introduced.

nodes.title: Multidisciplinary Capstone Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.description: This course allows the coordination of senior students in multiple departments while they undertake a multi-departmental capstone design project. Participating students are required to concurrently enroll in their respective departmental capstone/senior design project courses (ECE 189AB, CMPSC 189AB, ECE 188AB, ME 189ABC), and will additionally enroll in 1 unit of this course for the Fall, Winter and Spring quarters. By taking this course, students will understand practical engineering approaches to collaborate on complex multidisciplinary engineering systems.

nodes.title: Multidisciplinary Capstone Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Engineering 195A.
nodes.description: This course allows the coordination of senior students in multiple departments while they undertake a multi-departmental capstone design project. Participating students are required to concurrently enroll in their respective departmental capstone/senior design project courses (ECE 189AB, CMPSC 189AB, ECE 188AB, ME 189ABC), and will additionally enroll in 1 unit of this course for the Fall, Winter and Spring quarters. By taking this course, students will understand practical engineering approaches to collaborate on complex multidisciplinary engineering systems.

nodes.title: Multidisciplinary Capstone Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Engineering 195B
nodes.description: This course allows the coordination of senior students in multiple departments while they undertake a multi-departmental capstone design project. Participating students are required to concurrently enroll in their respective departmental capstone/senior design project courses (ECE 189AB, CMPSC 189AB, ECE 188AB, ME 189ABC), and will additionally enroll in 1 unit of this course for the Fall, Winter and Spring quarters. By taking this course, students will understand practical engineering approaches to collaborate on complex multidisciplinary engineering systems.

nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Math 3A with precalculus: A function approach integrating algebra, trigonometry, and differential calculus. Topics include: one-on-one and onto functions; inverse functions; properties and graphs of polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions; properties and graphs of trigonometric functions; analytic geometry; functions and limits; derivatives; techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Math 3B with precalculus: A continued review of relevant topics from precalculus (see Math 2A); integral calculus, including definite and indefinite integrals; techniques of integration, introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, First Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.

requires.text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam

nodes.description: Differential Calculus including analytic geometry, functions and limits, derivatives, techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.

nodes.title: Calculus with Applications, Second Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 3A with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Integral calculus including definite and indefinite integrals, techniques of integration; introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.

nodes.title: Linear Algebra with Applications
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Math 2B or 3B or 3BI with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, vector spaces and subspaces, basis and dimension, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization, and orthogonality.

nodes.title: Differential Equations
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Math 4A or Math 4AI with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: First and second order differential equations, separation of variables, linear differential equations, systems of first order equations, nonlinear differential equations and stability.

nodes.title: Vector Calculus with Applications, First Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A (or 4AI) with a letter grade of C or better.
nodes.description: Calculus of functions of several variables, vector valued functions of one variable, derivative and integrals of vector functions, double and triple integrals, properties and applications of integrals, change of variables.

nodes.title: Vector calculus with Applications, Second Course
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4B (or 4BI) and Mathematics 6A, each with a minimum grade of C.
nodes.description: Scalar and vector fields, integration along paths, integration over surfaces and solid regions, integral theorems of vector calculus, Fourier series, partial differential equations.

nodes.title: Structure and Properties I
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Chemistry 1A-B and Mathematics 4B, 6A, 6B
nodes.description: An introduction to materials in modern technology. The internal structure of materials and its underlying principles: bonding, spatial organization of atoms and molecules, structural defects. Electricial, magnetic and optical properties of materials, and their relationship with structure.

nodes.title: Structures and Properties II
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Materials 100A.
nodes.description: Mechanical properties of engineering materials and their relationship to bonding and structure. Elastic, flow, and fracture behavior; time dependent deformation and failure. Stiffening, strengthening, and toughening mechanisms. Thermo-mechanical interactions in materials.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Structural Evolution
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: Materials 100A and Materials 100B.
nodes.description: An introduction to the thermodynamic and kinetic principles governing structural evolution in materials. Phase equilibria, diffusion and structural transformations. Metastable structures in materials. Self-assembling systems. Structural control through processing and/ or imposed fields. Environmental effects on structure and properties.

nodes.title: Introduction to the Structure and Properties of Materials
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.description: Introduction to the structure of engineering materials and its relationship with their mechanical properties. Structure of solids and defects. Concepts of microstructure and origins. Elastic, plastic flow and fracture properties. Mechanisms of deformation and failure. Stiffening, strengthening, and toughening mechanisms.

nodes.title: Manufacturing and Materials
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 151C; and ME 15; and Materials 101 or Materials 100C
nodes.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of common manufacturing processes and their interplay with the structure and properties of materials as they are transformed into products. Emphasis on process understanding and the key physical concepts and basic mathematical relationships involved in each of the processes discussed.

nodes.title: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Introduction to additive manufacturing processes: review ofmanufacturing methods and process selection consideration, economies of production, common additive manufacturing strategies, and brief description of the physics of photopolymerization, extrusion, selective laser melting and e-beam melting fabrication.

nodes.title: Basic Electrical and Electronic Circuits
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7B, or Physics 3 and Physics 3L; and Mathematics 4A, or 4AI, or 3C; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Introduction to basic electrical circuits and electronics. Includes Kirchhoff's laws, phasor analysis, circuit elements, operational amplifiers and transistor circuits.

nodes.title: Engineering Graphics: Sketching, CAD and Conceptual Design
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Mechanical Engineering majors only.
nodes.description: Introduces hands-on engineering design via lessons on the design process, Computer Aided Design (CAD), free hand sketching, use of a laser cutter, soldering, basic circuits, basic microprocessor programming, motors and gear trains. Makes use of a robotic project to allow students to practice all above topics. Students create dimensioned engineering drawings and present their designs at a final design fair. The focus of the course is to empower students to leverage all engineering tools listed above in their future engineering courses.

nodes.title: Introduction to Machine Shop
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Mechanical engineering majors only.
nodes.description: Basic machine shop skills course. Students learn to work safely in a machine shop. Students are introduced to the use of hand tools, the lathe, the milling machine, drill press, saws, and precision measuring tools. Students apply these skills by completing a project.

nodes.title: Statics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Math 2B, or Math 3B, or AP Calculus AB with a score of 5, or AP Calculus BC with a score of 3 or better; and Physics 7A, or Physics 1

items.text: AP Calculus AB with a score of 5

nodes.description: Introduction to applied mechanics. Forces, moments, couples, and resultants; vector algebra; construction of free body diagrams; equilibrium in 2- and 3-dimensions; analysis of frames, machines, trusses and beams; distributed forces; friction.

nodes.title: Strength of Materials
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-; open to mechanical engineering majors only.

items.text: open to mechanical engineering majors only

nodes.description: Properties of structural materials, including Hookes law and behavior beyond the elastic limit. Concepts of stress, strain, displacement, force, force systems, and multiaxial stress states. Design applications to engineering structures, including problems of bars in tension, compression, and torsion, beams subject to flexure, pressure vessels, and buckling.

nodes.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7A or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C (may be taken concurrently); open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Vectorial kinematics of particles. Coordinate systems, moving frames, relative and constrained motion. Dynamics of particles and systems of particles. Energy and momentum methods. Collisions. Planar kinematics and kinematics of rigid bodies. Energy and momentum methods for rigid body systems.

nodes.title: Mathematics of Engineering
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Engineering 3; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Introduction to basic numerical and analytical methods, with implementation using MATLAB. Topics include a Matlab review, ordinary differential equations, partial differential equations and boundary conditions, eigenvalue/eigenvectors. Graphic and visualization tools in Matlab.

nodes.title: Finite Elements Analysis of Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow with COMSOL
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME151B and ME152A; or by consent of Instructor
nodes.description: Study of modeling and analysis of Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow problems using Finite Elements numerical techniques. Students learn to develop sound numerical models of engineering devices using COMSOL Multiphysics Finite Elements software. Addresses geometry construction, model development, meshing, results generation, and physical analysis.

nodes.title: Dynamical Systems
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: Math 6B and ME 16
nodes.description: Equations of Motion for Mechanical, Electrical, Heat, Fluid, and Control Systems. Block diagram algebra and interconnections. Laplace transform. Transfer functions and dynamic stability. First and second order systems. Frequency response. Introduction to mechanical vibrations and feedback control design.

nodes.title: Mechatronics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: ME 6 and ME 103; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Interfacing of mechanical and electrical systems and mechatronics. Basic introduction to sensors, actuators, and computer interfacing and control. Transducers and measurement devices, actuators, A/D and D/A conversion, signal conditioning and filtering. Practical skills developed in weekly lab exercises.

nodes.title: Mechanical Engineering Laboratory
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: ME 151B, ME 152A, ME 103; and MATRL 101 or MATRL 100C.
nodes.description: Introduction to fundamental engineering laboratory measurement techniques and report writing skills. Experiments from thermosciences, fluid mechanics, mechanics, and materials science. Introduction to modern data acquisition and analysis techniques.

nodes.title: Machine Learning
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: ME 17; or consent of instructor
nodes.description: Introduces students to machine learning and deep learning. ME 107 is taught at the undergraduate level and teaches students how to identify a machine learning problem in the context of real-world applications, mathematically formulate a learning problem, identify when a learning problem is well-posed, under-determined and overdetermined, and develop algorithms and Python code to solve the problem. Students are introduced to the concepts of learning algorithms, overfitting, under-fitting, statistical measures of estimators, optimization approaches to learning, principal component analysis, regression, support vector machines, and artificial neural networks.

nodes.title: Applications of Finite Element Analysis
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: ME 14; ME 15
nodes.description: Modeling and translation into practical FEA using SolidWorks simulation tools. The course focuses on choosing the correct constraints for parts and assembly. Another focus is on moving parts within SolidWorks. If time permits the class considers optimization of mechanical structures based on anticipated loads. This class goes through the cycle of designing, performing FEA, testing and repeat. SolidWorks, including its geometry optimization module, is used in this class as a calculator. This fulfills the need of industry (SolidWorks), while preparing students to Capstone and other courses.

nodes.title: Aerodynamics and Aeronautical Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Mechanical Engineering 14 and 152A
nodes.description: Concepts from aerodynamics, including lift and drag analysis for airfoils as well as aircraft sizing/scaling issues. Structural mechanics concepts are applied to practical aircraft design. Intended for students considering a career in aeronautical engineering.

nodes.title: Energy
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Senior Undergraduate or Graduate Student status in the College of Engineering; or consent of Instructor
nodes.description: Introduction to the field of Energetics. Topics may include energy sources and production, energy usage, renewable technologies, hardware, operating principles, environmental impact, energy reserves, national and global energy budgets, historical perspectives, economics, societal considerations, and others.

nodes.title: Soft Robotics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 16, ME 103, and ME 104
nodes.description: Learning from the versatility and robustness of bodies in nature, robotic devices are moving away from the traditional rigid form to designs that intentionally and carefully incorporate compliance. We explore this emerging paradigm of robots by 1) modeling the underlying mechanics of soft systems, such as soft actuators, sensors, and bodies, 2) examining current literature and gleaning design principles, and 3) designing and fabricating soft robotic devices in a hands-on laboratory setting. This course includes a final project; students are expected to design, model, fabricate, and test either a subcomponent or a full soft robot.

groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives

nodes.title: Introduction to Mechanisms
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 3
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16.
nodes.description: Generation, analysis, and refinement of the design of electro-mechanical devices for common machine elements including fasteners, joints, springs, bearings, gearing, motors, pneumatics, clutches, couplings, belts, chains, and shafts making use of physics, mathematics, and engineering principles.

nodes.title: Design of Biomedical Devices
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Mechanical Engineering 10, 14, 15, 16 or ME W 16, and 153; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Introductory course addresses the challenges of biomedical device design, prototyping and testing, material considerations, regulatory requirements, design control, human factors and ethics.

nodes.title: Manufacturing and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 3
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.description: Introduction to manufacturing, surveying a broad range of manufacturing methods and focusing on a few select processes. The course covers some of the considerations and decisions that go into process selection, manufacturing systems, design for manufacture, and design for assembly, as well as how those decisions influence manufacturing quality and cost.

nodes.title: Renewable Energy Technologies
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper division standing; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Focuses on emerging technologies to generate energy from renewable sources, harvest waste energy, and improve the efficiency of existing energy infrastructure. Three main categories of technologies will be discussed: solar energy, thermoelectrics, and solid-state cooling. Thermodynamic principles underlying these renewable energy technologies will be analyzed in detail. Engineering challenges and economic analysis will be provided when relevant.

nodes.title: Projects in Thermal Sciences
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of Instructor
nodes.description: The focus of the class is on Heat Transfer, Energetics, and Fluid Mechanics. The primary activity will be individual projects on topics selected by each student in associated areas such as Alternative Energy technologies, Manufacturing, HVAC, Engines, Electronic devices, etc. Topics may be related to Senior Capstone projects, professional work, Research, Engineering competitions or clubs, internships, etc. Intended for Juniors, Seniors, and Graduate students in Engineering and the Physics department, with enrollment subject to Instructor approval.

nodes.title: Wind and Tidal Energy
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 152A
nodes.description: Actuator disc theory; Blade element momentum theory; Design of optimal rotors; Wind turbine wakes; The atmosphere, and effects of atmospheric stability; Models of large wind farms; Open channel-flows; Energy available in tidal flows.

nodes.title: Numerical Analysis in Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 17 with a minimum grade of C-, or Chemical Engineering 132A.
nodes.description: Numerical analysis and analytical solutions of problems described by linear and nonlinear differential equations with an emphasis on MATLAB. First and second order differential equations; systems of differential equations; linear algebraic equations, matrices and eigenvalues; boundary value problems; finite differences.

groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives

nodes.title: Introduction to Nanoelectromechanical and Microelectromechanical systems (NEMS/MEMS)
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 4
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16 and 17; ME 152A and ME 151A (may be concurrent); or ECE 130A & 137A with a minimum grade of C- in both.
nodes.description: Introduction to nano- and microtechnology. Scaling laws and nanoscale physics are stressed. Individual subjects at the nanoscale including materials, mechanics, photonics, electronics, and fluidics will be described, with an emphasis on differences of behavior at the nanoscale and real-world examples.

nodes.title: MEMS: Processing and Device Characterization
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 4
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 141A or ECE 141A.
nodes.description: Lectures and laboratory on semiconductor-based processing for MEMS. Description of key equipment and characterization tools used for MEMS and design, fabrication, characterization and testing of MEMS. Emphasis on current MEMS devices including accelerometers, comb drives, micro-reactors and capacitor-actuators.

nodes.title: Molecular and Cellular Biomechanics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.description: Course introduces fundamental concepts in molecular and cellular biomechanics. Will consider the role of physical, thermal and chemical forces, examine their influence on cell strength and elasticity, and explore the properties of enzymatically-active materials.

groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives

nodes.title: Thermosciences 1
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7D or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C
nodes.description: Basic concepts in thermodynamics, system analysis, energy, thermodynamic laws, and cycles.

nodes.title: Thermosciences 2
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: ME 151A and 152A.
nodes.description: Introduction to heat transfer processes, steady and unsteady state conduction, multidimensional analysis. Introduction to convective heat transfer.

nodes.title: Thermosciences 3
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 6
nodes.prereq_text: ME 151B and 152A. Open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Convective heat transfer, external and internal flow, forced and free convection, phase change, heat exchangers. Introduction to radiative heat transfer.

nodes.title: Fluid Mechanics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: Math 6B or Math 5C, and ME 16 or ME W 16 with a minimum grade of C-, and Physics 7B or Physics 2
nodes.description: Introduction to the fundamental concepts in fluid mechanics and basic fluid properties. Basic equations of fluid flow. Dimensional analysis and similitude. Hydrodynamics.

nodes.title: Fluid Mechanics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 6
nodes.prereq_text: ME 152A. Open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Incompressible viscous flow. Turbomachinery. Boundary-layer theory. Introductory considerations for one-dimensional compressible flow.

nodes.title: Introduction to Mechanical Engineering Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: ME 10 and 16 or ME W 16; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: This course introduces engineering design with a focus on an iterative design process. Throughout the course, a group project cements the topics learned through active application to a real design problem. The lectures are broken into three sections. Section 1 introduces a version of this iterative Design Cycle, which comprises four components: 1) Define, 2) Ideate, 3) Prototype & Test, and 4) Analyze. These steps are repeated many times over the course of design development, not always in this order. Section 2 of the course focuses on applying this Design Cycle to the team project. Section 3 wraps up and focuses on presenting the project.

nodes.title: Design and Analysis of Structures
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 5
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 15 with a minimum grade of C-; and, ME 16 or ME W 16 with a minimum grade of C-; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Introductory course in structural analysis and design. The theories of matrix structural analysis and finite element analysis for the solution of analytical and design problems in structures are emphasized. Lecture material includes structural theory compatibility method, slope deflection method, displacement method, and virtual work. Topics include applications to bars, beams, trusses, frames, and solids.

nodes.title: Control System Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 2
nodes.prereq_text: ME 17 with a minimum grade of C-; ME 103.
nodes.description: The discipline of control and its application. Dynamics and feedback. The mathematical models: transfer functions and state space descriptions. Simple control design (PID). Assessment of a control problem, specification, fundamental limitations, codesign of system and control.

nodes.title: Advanced Control Systems Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 155A.
nodes.description: Dynamic system modeling using state-space methods, controllability and observability, state-space methods for control design including pole placement, and linear quadratic regulator methods. Observers and observer-based feedback controllers. Sampled-data and digital control. Laboratory exercises using MATLAB for simulation and control design.

nodes.title: Control Systems Laboratory
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 155A.
nodes.description: Advanced lab course with experiments in dynamical systems and feedback control design. Students design, troubleshoot, and perform detailed, multi-session experiments.

nodes.title: Mechanical Engineering Design - I
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: ME 14, with a minimum grade of C-; and ME 15, with a minimum grade of C-; and MATRL 101 (or MATRL 100B); or consent of instructor. Open to ME majors only
nodes.description: The rational selection of engineering materials, and the utilization of Ashby-charts, stress, strain, strength, and fatigue failure consideration as applied to the design of machine elements. Lectures also support the development of system design concepts using assigned projects and involve the preparation of engineering reports and drawings.

nodes.title: Mechanical Engineering Design-II
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: ME 156A. Open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Machine elements including gears, bearings and shafts. Joint design and analysis: bolts, rivets, adhesive bonding and welding. Machine dynamics andfatigue. Design reliability and safety. Codes and standards. Topics coveredwill be applies in practical design projects.

nodes.title: Introduction to Multiphysics Simulation
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Mechanical Engineering 151A-B; and Mechanical Engineering 152A-B
nodes.description: Introduces students to the concepts of multiphysics simulation. Students are introduced to PDEs, associated analytical solutions, and the finite elements method. Multiphysics problems are solved in multiple domains, and with fluid/structure interactions. Each student conducts a project where multiphysics tools are used to explore details of multiphysical processes.

nodes.title: Computer Aided Design and Manufacturing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 10 and ME 12S; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Emphasis on programming, operation and design of automated manufacturing tools. Students learn to program CNC tools to make parts with G&M Code and Mastercam CAM software. Students make parts in hands-on labs using CNC tools, 3D printers and laser cutters. Select topics in automated tool design and construction.

nodes.title: Introduction to Design Optimization
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Building a theoretical understanding of various optimization schemes and methods. Numerical simulation of physical design problems with a goal to optimize the design of a system and an emphasis on using COMSOL Multiphysics software package. Gradient-based and gradient-free minimization/maximization of objective functions; parameter optimization, shape optimization; topology optimization; inverse problem-solving.

groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives

nodes.title: Engineering Mechanics: Vibrations
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 2
nodes.prereq_text: ME 16 or ME W 16 with a minimum grade of C-; ME 103; open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Topics relating to vibration in mechanical systems; exact and approximate methods of analysis, matrix methods, generalized coordinates and Lagrange's equations, applications of systems. Basic feedback systems and controlled dynamic behavior.

nodes.title: Advanced Strength of Materials
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Group 5
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 15; instructor consent
nodes.description: Covers the mechanical behavior of engineering materials, with an emphasis on understanding the physical and microstructural origins of material response. Topics include the tensile test, elasticity, crystal structure and defects, phase diagrams, yield and plasticity, fracture mechanics, stress corrosion cracking, fatigue, cyclic crack growth, Weibull statistics, and creep. Theoretical frameworks are connected throughout to real engineering applications and design.

nodes.title: Structural Analysis
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 15
nodes.description: Presents introductory matrix methods for analysis of structures. Topics include review of matrix algebra and linear equations, basic structural theorems including the principle of superposition and energy theorems, truss bar, bean and plane frame elements, and programming techniques to realize these concepts.

nodes.title: Nonlinear Phenomena
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 105A or Physics 103; or ME 163 or upper-division standing in ECE.
nodes.description: Introduction to nonlinear phenomena. Flows and bifurcations in one and two dimensions, chaos, fractals, strange attractors. Applications to physics, engineering, chemistry, and biology.

nodes.title: Introduction to Robotics: Dynamics and Control
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ECE 130A or ME 103
nodes.description: Dynamic modeling and control methods for robotic systems. Lagrangian method for deriving equations of motion, introduction to the Jacobian, and modeling and control of forces and contact dynamics at a robotic end effector. Laboratories encourage a problem-solving approach to control.

nodes.title: Introduction to Robotics: Design Laboratory
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Engr 3; and ME 6 or ECE 2A. Not open for credit to students who have completed ME 170C or ECE 181C.

items.text: Not open for credit to students who have completed ME 170C

nodes.description: Design, programming, and testing of mobile robots. Design problems are formulated in terms of robot performance. Students solve electromechanical problems, developing skills in brainstorming, concept selection, spatial reasoning, teamwork and communication. Robots are controlled with micro-controllers using C programming and interfaced to sensors and motors.

nodes.title: Introduction to Robotics: Planning and Kinematics
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 4A and Upper-Division standing only.
nodes.description: Motion planning and kinematics topics with an emphasis on geometric reasoning, programming, and matrix computations. Motion planning: configuration spaces, sensor-based planning, decomposition and sampling methods, and advanced planning algorithms. Kinematics: reference frames, rotations and displacements, kinematic motion models.

nodes.title: Crystalline Defects
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Math 3B, ME 14, and ME 15.
nodes.description: An in-depth look into the many classes of defects (e.g., point, linear, and planar) and the role they play in crystalline materials. While we cannot eliminate defects and they are usually seen as a weakness, proper understanding of defects is the best way to design stronger and better materials. Examples of the types of defects we may cover are vacancies, dislocations, grain boundaries, interfaces, and twins. We will study their formation, mobility and interaction in environments where they are commonly found, such as elevated temperatures, mechanical strains, or irradiation.

nodes.title: Materials in Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Materials 100B or 101.
nodes.description: Introduces the main families of materials and the principles behind their development, selection, and behavior. Discusses the generic properties of metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites more relevant to structural applications. The relationship of properties to structure and processing is emphasized in every case.

nodes.title: Manufacturing and Materials
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 151C; and ME 15; and Materials 101 or Materials 100C
nodes.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of common manufacturing processes and their interplay with the structure and properties of materials as they are transformed into products. Emphasis on process understanding and the key physical and basic mathematical relationships involved in each of the processes discussed.

nodes.title: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Introduction to additive manufacturing processes: review ofmanufacturing methods and process selection consideration, economies of production, common additive manufacturing strategies, and brief description of the physics of photopolymerization, extrusion, selective laser melting and e-beam melting fabrication.

nodes.title: Capstone Mechanical Engineering Design Project
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: ME 103; and ME 151B; and ME 152A; and ME 153; or consent of instructor. Open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Students work in teams under the direction of a faculty advisor (and possibly an industrial sponsor) to tackle an engineering design project. Engineering communication, such as reports and oral presentations, are covered. Emphasis on practical, hands-on experience, and the integration of analytical and design skills.

nodes.title: Capstone Mechanical Engineering Design Project
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: ME 189A
nodes.description: Students work in teams under the direction of a faculty advisor (and possibly an industrial sponsor) to tackle an engineering design project. Engineering communication, such as reports and oral presentations, are covered. Course emphasizes practical, hands-on experience, and integrates analytical and design skills acquired in the companion ME 156 courses.

nodes.title: Capstone Mechanical Engineering Design Project
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Required Courses
nodes.prereq_text: ME 189A and 189B
nodes.description: Students work in teams under the direction of a faculty advisor (and possibly an industrial sponsor) to tackle an engineering design project. Engineering communication, such as reports and oral presentations, are covered. Course emphasizes practical, hands-on experience, and integrates analytical and design skills acquired in the companion ME 156 courses.

nodes.title: Independent Projects in Mechanical Engineering Design
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: ME 16; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Special projects in design engineering. Course offers motivated students opportunity to synthesize academic skills by designing and building new machines.

nodes.title: Independent Studies in Mechanical Engineering
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; upper-division standing; completion of two upper-division courses in Mechanical Engineering.

items.text: completion of two upper-division courses in Mechanical Engineering

nodes.description: Directed individual study.

nodes.title: Engineering Mechanics: Dynamics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7A or Physics 2, and ME 14 with a minimum grade of C-, and Math 6B or Math 5C (may be taken concurrently); open to ME majors only.
nodes.description: Vectorial kinematics of particles. Coordinate systems, moving frames, relative and constrained motion. Dynamics of particles and systems of particles. Energy and momentum methods. Collisions. Planar kinematics and kinematics of rigid bodies. Energy and momentum methods for rigid body systems.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Introduction to classical mechanics for students in engineering and the physical sciences. Measurement, units, and foundations of physics; vectors; kinematics; circular motion; forces, mass, and Newton's laws; center of mass; momentum; work and energy; conservation laws; collisions; rotational kinematics.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 1 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Rotational dynamics and angular momentum; equilibrium and elasticity; periodic motion including LRC electrical circuits; gravitation; fluid mechanics; temperature; thermal expansion; heat and the first law of thermodynamics; heat conduction; kinetic theory of gases; entropy and the second law; heat engines.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 2 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B (AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better) and 4A.

items.text: AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Mechanical waves, wave interference and normal modes, sound and hearing, electric field, Gauss's law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.

nodes.title: Physics Laboratory
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 3 or 23 (may be taken concurrently).
nodes.description: Introductory laboratory emphasizing periodic motion, sound and basic electronics.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 3 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.

nodes.title: Basic Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Kinematics in 3D, Newton’s Laws, Energy, Momentum and Collisions, Rotation, Statics and Equilibrium

nodes.title: Basic Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7A with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Gravity, Periodic Motion and Oscillations, Mechanical Waves and Sound, Coulomb’s Law, Electric Field and Gauss’s Law, Electric Potential, DC circuits

nodes.title: Basic Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7B with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

items.text: AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Magnetic Forces and Field, Induction, Inductance and AC circuits, Maxwell’s equations and E/M waves, Geometric and Physical Optics

nodes.title: Basic Physics
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7C with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B (AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better) and 4A.

items.text: AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better

nodes.description: Temperature, Heat, Laws of Thermodynamics, Special Relativity, Photons, Wave-particle duality of Matter, Intro to Quantum Mechanics, Schrodinger Equation in 1D, Hydrogen Atom.

nodes.title: Physics Laboratory
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower-Division
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 7B; Co-requisite: Physics 7C
nodes.description: Periodic motion, sound, and basic electronics, while emphasizing good laboratory techniques such as uncertainty propagation, statistical analysis, developing and testing models, and good report writing.

nodes.title: Introduction to Mathematical Methods for Physics
nodes.description: Single variable functions, derivatives and integrals with applications to kinematics. Taylor series. Introduction to ordinary differential equations and Newtons second law as an ODE. Vectors and scalars with physics applications. Dot and cross products. Matrices and determinants. Unit circle and trigonometric identities. Polar coordinates and kinematics in polar coordinates.

nodes.title: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Mathematics 2A/3A and Mathematics 2B/3B or Physics 8 or AP Calculus BC Exam score of 5.
nodes.description: Classical mechanics, kinematics, vectors, Newtons laws, work and energy, conservation laws, rotational kinematics.

nodes.title: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 21 with a grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Rotational dynamics, fluid mechanics, gravitation, periodic motion, temperature and heat, thermodynamics.

nodes.title: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 22 with a minimum grade of C- or better.
nodes.description: Mechanical waves, sound, electric charge and electric field, Gauss Law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.

nodes.title: General Physics
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 23 with a minimum grade of C-; Mathematics 4A.
nodes.description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.

nodes.title: Intermediate Mechanics and Special Relativity
nodes.prereq_text: Physics 2 or 22 with a minimum grade of C-. Mathematics 6A (may be taken concurrently)
nodes.description: Newtonian mechanics in 3D. Conservation laws. Complex numbers. Oscillations. Inertial reference frames, Lorentz transformations, relativistic momentum and energy, four-vectors.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Business Strategy
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Sophomore standing or higher.
nodes.description: An introduction to business strategy, principles and practices required for business success in the competitive market place. Students are exposed to key management theories, models and tools including competitive strategy, finance, planning, new product development, marketing, leadership and others.

nodes.title: Entrepreneurship
groups: UPPER DIVISION MAJOR: Approved Engineering Electives
nodes.prereq_text: Sophomore standing or higher.
nodes.description: Learn how to start any type of venture; for profit, non-profit, service, sole-proprietorship, with a focus on high-tech ventures. Analysis of new business opportunities, development of customer-centric value propositions, financing, marketing, selling, and protection of intellectual property.
